By default it reads the segmented cells (per-cell count matrix and cell
boundary polygons) that Space Ranger 4.x writes to `segmented_outputs/`. Set
`--mode bins` to instead read a binned output (`binned_outputs/square_<N>um/`)
at the bin size given by `--bin_size`. In both cases the loaded table is
renamed to "table" so that downstream components stay technology-agnostic.



## Argument group

### Arguments

|Name             |Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |Attributes                                         |
|:----------|:--------------------------------------------------|:--------------------|
|`--input`        |Input folder containing the output from a Space Ranger run for Visium HD and a `*_feature_slice.h5` file. Must contain a `segmented_outputs/` directory for `--mode segmented_cells`, or `binned_outputs/` for `--mode bins`. |`file`, required, example: `"spaceranger_output"`  |
|`--output`       |Zarr directory where the SpatialData object will be stored.                                                                                                                                                                   |`file`, required, example: `"visium_hd_data.zarr"` |
|`--mode`         |Which output to load into the table: `segmented_cells` (per-cell counts and cell boundary polygons from `segmented_outputs/`) or `bins` (binned counts from `binned_outputs/square_<bin_size>um/`).                           |`string`, default: `"segmented_cells"`             |
|`--bin_size`     |Bin size in microns to load when `--mode bins`. Visium HD captures data at 2 µm and aggregates it into 8 µm and 16 µm square bins.                                                                                            |`integer`, default: `8`                            |
|`--output_type`  |Which count matrix to load: `filtered` (barcodes under tissue only) or `raw` (all barcodes). Applies to both the segmented-cell and binned matrices.                                                                          |`string`, default: `"filtered"`                    |
|`--output_layer` |If provided, the count matrix is also stored as a named layer (`table.layers[output_layer]`) in addition to `.X`.                                                                                                             |`string`                                           |
|`--dataset_id`   |Identifier used to name the spatial elements (shapes and images) in the SpatialData object. If not provided, it is inferred from the `*_feature_slice.h5` file name in the input directory.                                   |`string`                                           |

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/convert/from_spaceranger_hd_to_spatialdata/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

<details>
<summary>Example of `params.yaml`</summary>

Generate a `params.yaml` for this component on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/components/convert/from_spaceranger_hd_to_spatialdata).

</details>

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/convert/from_spaceranger_hd_to_spatialdata/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

:::{.callout-note}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend.
:::

Running on Seqera or through Viash Hub is explained in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
